header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Endure Hardships and difficulties when Giving Da'wah towards Allaah

blocks.text: Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) as he was being tortured and calling out "Ahad" ("Allaah is One"), he would say, "Allaah is One, O Bilaal." Waraqa bin Naufal would then turn to Umayyah bin Khalaf who was responsible for torturing Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and say, "I swear by Allaah that if you kill this man, I shall definitely make his grave a place of attracting Allaah's blessings and mercy."

Eventually, when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed by one day as the Mushrikeen were torturing Hadhrat Bilaal (RA), he said to Umayyah, "Do you not fear Allaah for (what you are doing to) this poor man? Until when will you continue?" Umayyah said, "It is you who had landed him into this trouble. You may rescue him from this treatment you are witnessing." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "I am prepared to do so. I have an Abyssinian slave who is stronger than him and more steadfast on your religion. I shall give him to you in exchange for this man." When Umayyah accepted the proposal, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "You have a deal." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then gave Umayyah the slave and after taking possession of Hadhrat Bilaal (RA), set him free. Before migrating to Madinah, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) set free seven slaves besides Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) for the pleasure of Allaah.[^1]

A narration of Ibn Is'haaq states that when the afternoon heat grew intense, Umayyah would take Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) outside and throw him down on the burning sands of Makkah. He would then command others to place a heavy rock on the chest of Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and say to him, "You shall be left like this until you die or reject Muhammad and worship Laat and Uzza!" Despite his extreme suffering, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) would continuously say, "Ahad! Ahad!"

Speaking about the torture that Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and the others suffered and about how Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) freed them (because of which Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) received the title of "Ateeq" from Rasulullaah ﷺ, meaning "The one freed from Jahannam") Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) used to recite some couplets (which mean):

On behalf of Bilaal and his companions, may Allaah abundantly reward
Ateeq and humiliate Faakih[^2] and Abu Jahal
I shall never forget the night when the two of them resolved to hurt Bilaal
Without having a concern for doing the evil that intelligent men stay far from
They tortured him only because of his belief in the Oneness of the Rabb of all creation and because of his statement
'I testify that Allaah is my Rabb and my heart is content with this'
'If they kill me, let them kill me but I shall never
associate partners with Ar Rahmaan because of fear for death'
O the Rabb of Ibraheem, Yunus
Moosa and Isa, rescue me and do not let me be tested
by those from the family of Ghaalib who continue plunging into deviation
Faakih bin Mughiera, the paternal uncle of Abu Jahal.
